idiom_name: thirtyfour Component derive: WebElement base + ElementResolver fields
implementation_notes: thirtyfour, the Rust WebDriver client, ships the closest thing to a page object: #[derive(Component)] on a struct with a base: WebElement field and #[by(css = "...")] field: ElementResolver<WebElement> fields, where resolve().await? re-queries on every call so components survive stale-element conditions, and component methods express the page's services as ordinary async Rust. Without the derive, the pattern is a hand-written struct holding WebDriver/WebElement and re-querying per action; with it, the derive macro replaces the classic Java page-object plumbing while the structure (one type per surface, methods returning values) stays the same. Choose the derive when thirtyfour is already the driver.
pitfalls: Rust has no async destructors: without an explicit driver.quit().await the executor blocks while shutting the session down (thirtyfour documents this).
Base and resolver elements can be stale like any WebElement; always go through resolve().await instead of keeping a resolved element in a field.
Component wrappers assume the root element stays on the page; after navigation, construct a new component from a fresh query rather than reusing the old struct.
